item.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
item.description: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. item.description: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. item.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
item.description: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.

item.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
Clay helps sales teams win with Codex and ChatGPT
item.description: ChatGPT and Codex integrations help Clay’s users research deals and turn data into go-to-market plays, with GPT-6 models handling the reasoning.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.

item.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
item.description: Watch OpenAI’s Stacey Wang and Craig Bruney, Mary O’Carroll of LECG, and Cooley’s Richard Segal explore how AI can help in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows and get more from outside counsel.

item.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
item.description: Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for their conversations.

item.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
item.description: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
